title: ca-fish-planting-alerts snapshot v1
description: One static file, regenerated by the pipeline, holding every plant the pipeline has ever observed on CDFW's Fish Planting Schedule, per water. A plant is a WEEK (Sunday..Saturday), never a day: CDFW publishes week-of granularity only. Consumers must never render a plant as a single date.

generated_at.description: When the pipeline built this file (UTC).

fetched_at.description: When the source page was fetched (UTC). The page is fetched at most once per run.

stated_today.description: Despite the name, the start (a Sunday) of CDFW's current week as the page itself states it -- the first date of its 'Current-Future Plants' range, which stays the same all week (a page fetched on Thursday 2026-09-17 states 2026-09-13). It is not the fetch day; see fetched_at for that. Freshness is judged from this, not from HTTP headers: unless it is the week of the run date (+/- 1 day of clock skew at the week boundary), the page is refused and no snapshot is built.

stated_period.description: The page's own 'All Plants (start - end)' window. Rows outside it are impossible; weeks that fall out of it age out of the page but never out of this file.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the fetched HTML, for reproducibility.

source_week.description: The CDFW week (Sunday..Saturday) that contains source.stated_today. 'This week' everywhere means this week.

text.description: Show this verbatim wherever data from this file is displayed.

species.description: Every species string ever observed, verbatim from CDFW (today: 'Trout', 'Catfish').

waters.description: Every water with at least one observed plant, sorted by id. Waters CDFW lists but has never planted in the observed window are not included.

this_week.description: Convenience index: plants whose week == source_week and whose status is 'listed'. Derived from waters[].plants; the pipeline tests that the two agree. May be empty on a fresh, valid page (a real 'no plants this week'); it is never emitted from a stale or failed fetch because no snapshot is built then.

waters_known.description: Waters in CDFW's own water list on the page (895 on 2026-09-13).

names_matched.description: Distinct (stock id, published name) pairs this run that already existed in the alias table.

date.description: ISO calendar date, America/Los_Angeles civil date.

water_id.description: 'cdfw-' + CDFW's own StockingWaterID (the stockid in the schedule's map links). Stable: it is CDFW's key, not ours.

start.description: Always a Sunday (CDFW's week runs Sunday..Saturday).

label.description: Display form. Never shorten to a single day.

status.description: 'listed': present on the most recent fresh page that covered this week. 'removed': CDFW listed it, then dropped it while the week was still inside the page's stated period (plants are 'subject to change'). Never inferred from a stale or failed fetch, and never for the period's oldest week, which the page ages off day by day while still stating the same period.

name.description: Display name. From the alias table when reviewed; otherwise CDFW's most recent spelling, verbatim.

slug.description: URL segment for the site's per-water page (site/water/<slug>/). Assigned once in the alias table and never changed.

aliases.description: Every spelling CDFW has published for this id.

region.description: Region of the first listed county (CDFW's own county->region mapping).

source.description: The licensed dataset the point came from. Coordinates are never guessed; absent a licensed source this is null.

last_listed_week.description: Newest week with status 'listed' whose start is <= source_week.start (i.e. not a future plant). Null if every observed plant is in the future.

plants.description: Every (week, species) ever observed for this water, oldest first. Append-only over time: an entry never disappears from a later snapshot.
